I'd be happy to help you get started with affiliate marketing! Here's a step-by-step guide to becoming an affiliate:

1. Choose Your Niche

Pick a topic you're knowledgeable or passionate about. Popular niches include:
  • Tech & Software (high commissions, recurring revenue)
  • Health & Wellness (evergreen demand)
  • Finance & Investing (high-ticket items)
  • Fashion & Beauty (visual, social-media friendly)
  • Home & Garden (broad audience)
  • Online Education (growing market)
Tip: The sweet spot is a niche with decent demand but not oversaturated.

2. Pick Your Platform

Where will you share content?
  • Blog/Website – Best for SEO and long-term passive income
  • YouTube – Great for tutorials and reviews
  • Social Media (Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest) – Fast growth potential
  • Email Newsletter – High conversion rates
  • Podcast – Trust-building medium

3. Find Affiliate Programs

Major Networks (join multiple programs in one place):
  • Amazon Associates – Easy to start, low commissions (1-10%)
  • ShareASale – Thousands of merchants
  • CJ Affiliate (Commission Junction) – Big brands
  • Impact – Modern platform, great for SaaS
  • Rakuten – Retail-focused
  • Awin – Strong in Europe
Direct Programs (often higher commissions):
  • Many companies run their own affiliate programs. Check the footer of websites for "Affiliates" or "Partners" links.

4. Create Valuable Content

Don't just drop links—solve problems:
  • Product reviews (honest, balanced)
  • Comparison posts ("X vs Y")
  • How-to tutorials featuring the product
  • Best-of roundups ("Best tools for...")
  • Case studies showing real results

5. Drive Traffic

  • SEO – Target long-tail keywords (e.g., "best running shoes for flat feet 2026")
  • Social media – Consistent posting, engage with your audience
  • Paid ads – Only once you know what converts
  • Email list – Build a list for direct access to your audience

6. Track & Optimize

  • Use tracking links to see what converts
  • A/B test different calls-to-action
  • Focus on what works, cut what doesn't
Quick question to help me tailor advice: What niche or industry are you most interested in? And do you already have a platform (blog, social media, YouTube, etc.) or are you starting from scratch?

Here's the dead-simple way to upload your index.html to GitHub and get a live link:

1. Create a GitHub Account

  • Go to github.com
  • Click Sign up → follow the steps (email, password, username)
  • Verify your email

2. Create a New Repository

  1. Click the + button (top right) → New repository
  2. Repository name: type Kayovee-Links
  3. Make sure it's set to Public
  4. Check the box: Add a README file
  5. Click Create repository

3. Upload Your index.html File

  1. In your new repo, click Add file → Upload files
  2. Click choose your files → select your index.html from Desktop
  3. Scroll down → click Commit changes

4. Turn On GitHub Pages

  1. Click Settings (top menu, next to Insights)
  2. In the left sidebar, click Pages
  3. Under Source, change from None to Deploy from a branch
  4. Under Branch, select main → folder / (root) → click Save
  5. Wait 1–2 minutes, then refresh the page

5. Get Your Live Link
